title: fix(app-shell): the flow inspector's fallback form writes only keys the node contract declares (objectui#11968)
body:
Fixes #11968

Clause-②: no — this removes one written key and renames another to the key the contract already declares; no published surface widens (triage's reading on the card).

## What changes

Studio's flow-node inspector renders the hand-written `FLOW_NODE_CONFIG` groups (the fallback form) whenever the engine has published no `configSchema` for a node type: while `GET /automation/actions` is loading, and when it answers non-ok or throws. Two groups wrote config keys their node's contract does not declare:

- **HTTP request** offered an **Output variable** row writing `config.outputVariable`. The `http` executor never reads it, `HttpConfigSchema` is strict and refuses it by name, and the engine's registration refuses a flow carrying it, so a fallback edit saved a flow that then never registered. The row is removed; the online form never offered it.
- **Notify**'s **Click-through URL** row wrote `config.url`, the converted spelling of `actionUrl`. It now writes `actionUrl`, the key `NotifyConfigSchema` declares and the online form writes.

A flow that already stores either key still opens: the key shows in the Advanced (JSON) block, an unrelated edit keeps it unchanged, and clearing it there leaves a config the contract accepts. Until the author clears it, registration refuses that flow exactly as it did before.

## The pin

`flow-node-config.contractKeys-11968.test.tsx` holds every fallback group to its node's contract, read from the installed `@objectstack/spec` at test time — no contract is hand-copied:

- Every key a group can introduce is judged: each field path, plus each `objectList` column under the list element. A `config` key is judged against the config contract of every spec node type the inspector resolves to that group (`fieldsForNodeType` is alias-aware, so `http_request` is judged as the `http` node it renders for). Any other root (a sibling block, node-level `timeoutMs`) is judged against `FlowNodeSchema`. A `[REMOVED]` tombstone counts as undeclared.
- Contract sources: `getBuiltinNodeConfigContracts()`, `SCHEMALESS_NODE_CONFIG_SCHEMAS`, `LEDGER_DECLARED_NODE_CONFIG_SCHEMAS`. Two associations are made by name because the spec exports no table for them, with the key sets still read from the spec: `end` to `EndConfigSchema`, and the approval node type to `ApprovalNodeConfigSchema`.
- Exempt, each re-measured so an exemption cannot outlive its reason: fields behind the never-matching `__legacy__` controller (render-only, they cannot introduce a key); the decision `target` column (virtual, stripped by `applyDecisionBranches`); and the two groups no published contract judges, `start` and `legacy_action`.
- Lit controls in the same file show the walk fires at the top level, in a nested block, in an array element, in a sibling block and on a tombstone, and an accounting case requires every group to be judged, write no config key, or sit in the no-contract register. Each finding names the group, the node type and the key.
- The rendered half reads a flow that already stores a removed key (above), and that the zh overlay follows the renamed notify row.

## Files outside the claim's original surface

Seat ruling A on my report (comment 6062596737), recorded in the seat's ACCEPT, extended claim 6060906675 by these three, as a bounded in-place amendment. They are in their own commit 8f32f89ba:

- `FlowNodeInspector.requiredMarkers-10948.test.tsx`: its http row listed the removed Output variable label, and its aria-required case used that row's placeholder as the optional sibling. The sibling is now the Body text control.
- `FlowNodeInspector.declaredUnmapped-11788.test.tsx`: its "not brought back online" case read the offline notify `url` row, which no longer exists. It reads a fixture schema that leaves out `topic` instead, with the full schema as its lit control.
- `metadata-admin/i18n.ts`, `FLOW_FIELD_ZH` hunks only: the notify overlay is re-keyed `url` to `actionUrl` so the renamed row keeps its zh label on both forms, and the dead http `outputVariable` overlay goes. objectui#11977 adds rows to this file in another region; whichever lands second merges `main`.

## Evidence, at head 1aaf06f24

- Every test importing `flow-node-config` or naming `FlowNodeInspector` (57 files, the new pin included) plus `packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/column-identity.ratchet.test.ts`, repo-root `pnpm exec vitest run`, under the verify lock: `Test Files  58 passed (58)`, `Tests  904 passed | 1 skipped (905)`. Before the out-of-surface commit the same set read 2 files and 3 tests failed, the three cases named above.
- Ablation, committed state, through `ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode. A first attempt was a no-op: the replacement contained its anchor, the tool refused and restored, and no test ran. That reading is void. It was redone with another anchor:
  - Leg A (re-add the http Output variable row): `Tests  4 failed | 12 passed (16)`, and the main case printed `http_request (node type 'http') writes config.outputVariable: 'outputVariable' is not declared by its config contract`.
  - Leg B (notify row back to `url`): `Tests  5 failed | 11 passed (16)`, naming `notify (node type 'notify') writes config.url`.
  - Each leg was restored with the blob equal to HEAD and `git diff HEAD` empty.
  - Those legs ran at 8f32f89ba, where `flow-node-config.ts` is byte-identical to the head. The head commit then changed the findings' wording from "by" to "in".
- `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...'`: `Tasks: 28 successful, 28 total`. `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` exits 0; it runs `tsc --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, and `--listFilesOnly` lists all three touched test files.
- Gates, all exit 0: `check:spec-symbols`, `check:metadata-write-doors`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new citations), `check:control-bytes`, `check-changeset-presence.mjs`, `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, `check:test-path-roots`, the three `check:vi-mock-*`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:i18n-designer-parity`, `check:designer-field-key-parity` and `check:unreferenced-sources`. `eslint` on the 5 touched ts/tsx files: 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- NOT MEASURED locally:
  - `check:spec-floors`: it needs a whole-workspace build and reported no-artifact for every package, so it judged nothing here.
  - The eager-closure budget reading is left to CI.

## Acceptance notes

None of these was filed:

- `flow-scope` `nodeOutputRefs` adds `config.outputVariable` for every node type, and its comment lists http and end among the binders. A stored http or end node carrying the undeclared key therefore offers a data-picker variable the engine never binds, and the flow simulator binds it the same way. It is a reader of a key that registration refuses, not a writer, and its reach was not measured. Carrier: none.
- `FlowNodeInspector.endOutputVariable-9335.test.tsx` has a comment saying the spec declares the key on the http group. That was never true, and the row is now gone. Test comment only. Carrier: none.
- `apps/console/src/preview-samples.ts`, a dev-only sample, still carries an http node with `outputVariable`. It does not write stored metadata. Carrier: none.
- Read-only inference, NOT MEASURED: `HttpConfigSchema` declares `config.timeoutMs`, while both forms write node-level `timeoutMs`. `mergeServerFlowFields` drops the served config field in favour of the node-level one. Which of the two the http executor reads was not measured. Carrier: none.
- The spec publishes no contract for start-node config, and exports no table for the end and approval associations, so this pin names those two by hand. This is an observation for the spec lane, not a claimed defect.
